cost.hard_psf.detached_new.label: Build cost per sq ft, new detached backyard home
cost.hard_psf.detached_new.note: Building only, standard finish, 600 sq ft, in the Pennsylvania default cost area (area cost factor 1.09). Site work, utilities, contingency and soft costs are added separately. Set so that the all-in mid for 600 sq ft lands near 330 per sq ft in Philadelphia and 310 in Pittsburgh, the middle of what the sources below report for small Northeast units. No Pennsylvania survey of ADU costs exists.

sources.title: Block Renovation: ADU construction costs (500 sq ft about 350 per sq ft all-in, 800 sq ft about 275, national 150 to 400)
MassCEC ADU budgeting guide (250 to 500 per sq ft placeholder, hard cost about 85 percent of budget)
Cost to Build House: ADU cost in Pennsylvania (600 sq ft: Philadelphia 313 to 363, Pittsburgh 297 per sq ft all-in)
NAHB Cost of Constructing a Home 2024 (about 162 per sq ft construction cost for a large house, a floor)
Terner Center California ADU survey (median 250 per sq ft, 2020 prices)

cost.hard_psf.attached.label: Build cost per sq ft, attached addition
cost.hard_psf.attached.note: Shares a wall and often a foundation edge with the house. Sources say savings over detached are small.

sources.title: MassCEC ADU budgeting guide (2 bedroom attached 235k to 360k vs detached 250k to 450k)
Maxable: what does an ADU cost (attached about 200k, minimal savings vs detached)

cost.hard_psf.over_garage.label: Build cost per sq ft, unit over a garage
cost.hard_psf.over_garage.note: Second story on an existing garage. Structure, stairs and fire separation make it the costliest type per sq ft.

sources.title: Maxable: what does an ADU cost (above garage about 300k, most expensive type)
Angi: adding a room above a garage (80k to 210k)

cost.hard_psf.garage_conversion.label: Build cost per sq ft, garage conversion
cost.hard_psf.garage_conversion.note: Reuses the shell. Older Pennsylvania garages often need a new slab, insulation and roof work, so the high end is close to new construction.

sources.title: Angi: cost to convert a garage to an ADU (58k to 173k)
MassCEC ADU budgeting guide (garage conversions not much less than new construction)

cost.hard_psf.internal.label: Build cost per sq ft, conversion inside the house (basement, attic, floor)
cost.hard_psf.internal.note: Adds a kitchen, bath, separate entry and fire separation inside existing space.

sources.title: Angi: how much does an ADU cost (basement or attic 60k to 150k)
MassCEC ADU budgeting guide (interior conversion 120k to 270k)

cost.size_curve.label: Size effect on build cost per sq ft
cost.size_curve.unit: multiplier on cost.hard_psf, by unit size in sq ft
cost.size_curve.note: Kitchen, bath, heating and the panel cost about the same in any size, so small units cost more per sq ft. Linear between points, flat beyond the ends. Calibrated so all-in cost per sq ft (with the fixed site, utility and fee items) falls about 25 percent from 500 to 800 sq ft, as Block Renovation reports.

sources.title: Block Renovation: 500 sq ft about 350 per sq ft vs 800 sq ft about 275

cost.area_cost_factor.label: Area cost factor by place
cost.area_cost_factor.note: Build cost per sq ft is set for the reference area (Pennsylvania default 1.09). A place is scaled by its factor over the reference. Philadelphia is 7.3 percent above. Allegheny County and almost every other county use the state default. Harrisburg, Carlisle and Lebanon are 1.00 to 1.01, so the rest-of-state value is a little high there. RSMeans city indexes are paywalled.

sources.title: DoD UFS 3-701-01 Area Cost Factors 2026, Table 4-1 CONUS

cost.quality.label: Finish level
cost.quality.note: No source splits ADU cost by finish. Owner judgement.

cost.site_work.label: Site work (grading, foundation prep, access, tree removal)
cost.site_work.note: Detached from Block Renovation (slope or access 5k to 15k, soil 5k to 15k, tree 2k to 4k). Other types scaled down by judgement.

cost.utility_connection.label: Utility runs (water, sewer lateral, electric service or panel upgrade)
cost.utility_connection.note: Detached: Block Renovation 15k to 30k for all utilities. Low end from HomeAdvisor sewer line average 3,319 plus a 100 to 200 amp panel upgrade 1,300 to 2,000 plus trenching. Shorter runs for the other types (judgement).

cost.septic_upgrade.label: Septic upgrade where the lot is not on public sewer
cost.septic_upgrade.note: Only added when the lot has no public sewer (flag septic). Low is a conventional system, high a sand mound. Penn State Extension says these costs have not been quantified.

sources.title: Septic and Well: septic installation cost in Pennsylvania

cost.contingency.label: Contingency
cost.contingency.unit: share of build, site and utility cost
cost.contingency.note: Builders advise 10 to 20 percent. Use the high end for old garages and rowhouse basements.

sources.title: Case Design: contingency budget for residential construction (5 to 15 percent)

soft.design.label: Design and engineering
soft.design.note: Lower with a pre-approved or prefab plan.

sources.title: HomeAdvisor: architect fees (8 to 15 percent of construction)
MassCEC ADU budgeting guide (design 10 to 20 percent)

soft.survey.label: Boundary survey
soft.survey.note: Added for types that put a new footprint on the lot (cost.survey_types).

sources.title: Find Land Surveyor: land survey cost in Philadelphia County

cost.survey_types.label: ADU types that need a boundary survey
cost.survey_types.note: Setbacks are checked against lot lines only for a new footprint.

soft.permits.philadelphia.label: Philadelphia permit fees
soft.permits.philadelphia.unit: USD fixed plus share of build cost
soft.permits.philadelphia.note: Fixed: building permit for a new 1 to 2 family dwelling 1,328 + plumbing 284 + underground service 253 + zoning permit 189. Electrical permit is 25 per 1,000 of electrical work. Electrical work is taken as 10 percent of build cost (assumption), so 0.25 percent. A zoning board appeal adds 265 plus legal costs, not included.

sources.title: Philadelphia L&I PG_012 summary of construction permit fees, effective 2026-10-01
Philadelphia PZ_008 summary of zoning permit fees

soft.permits.pittsburgh.label: Pittsburgh permit fees
soft.permits.pittsburgh.unit: USD fixed plus share of build cost
soft.permits.pittsburgh.note: PLI residential base permit 6.00 per 1,000 of construction value, minimum 130, maximum 8,000. The zoning review fee was not found and is not included.

sources.title: City of Pittsburgh PLI 2026 fee schedule, effective 2026-01-01

soft.permits.rest_of_pa.label: Permit fees elsewhere in Pennsylvania
soft.permits.rest_of_pa.unit: USD fixed plus share of build cost
soft.permits.rest_of_pa.note: Each town sets its own Uniform Construction Code fees. The Pittsburgh schedule is used as a stand-in.

sources.title: City of Pittsburgh PLI 2026 fee schedule (stand-in)

soft.tap_fees.label: Water and sewer connection and tap fees
soft.tap_fees.note: Philadelphia Water: 3/4 inch ferrule tap 245 + 5/8 inch meter set 360 (FY27). No capacity fee found. Pittsburgh Water: permit 40 + 1 inch service and meter 570. Tapping fees ended in 2022. Elsewhere the local sewer authority sets a tap-in fee (North Huntingdon charges 5,500). Only added for types that get a new service (cost.new_service_types).

sources.title: Philadelphia Water Department FY26 and FY27 connection charges

cost.new_service_types.label: ADU types that need a new water and sewer service
cost.new_service_types.note: Attached and internal units usually branch off the house service.

soft.construction_tax.philadelphia.label: Philadelphia tax on residential construction
soft.construction_tax.philadelphia.note: Bill 200556 (2020) set a 1 percent tax on residential construction from 2022. The enacted rate and whether it reaches a small accessory unit were not verified. Kept in mid and high to stay on the safe side.

sources.title: Ballard Spahr: Philadelphia zoning, land use and construction update

rents.source.label: Market rent source

table.dataset: HUD Small Area Fair Market Rents

rents.source.note: ZIP level, 0 to 4 bedrooms, gross rent (rent plus tenant utilities) at the 40th percentile of recent movers. A ZIP in two FMR areas takes the lower rent. FY2026 applies 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30. The open service still held FY2026 when read on 2026-11-10.

sources.title: HUD PDR Small Area Fair Market Rents, open feature service

rents.fallback.label: Rent fallback where a ZIP has no SAFMR

table.dataset: ACS 2020-24 table B25031 median gross rent by bedrooms, tract

rents.fallback.note: Used for tract-level results and for PO box or new ZIPs without a SAFMR. Tract medians cover all renters (old and new leases) and are noisy for small bedroom groups.

rents.bedroom_cuts_sqft.label: Unit size to bedroom count
rents.bedroom_cuts_sqft.note: Under 450 sq ft rents as a studio, 450 to under 750 as 1 bedroom, 750 and up as 2 bedrooms.

rents.rent_factor.label: ADU rent as a share of the SAFMR
rents.rent_factor.note: A new unit rents above the 40th percentile, but the SAFMR includes tenant utilities. The two are taken to cancel.

financing.pmms30.label: 30-year fixed mortgage rate, latest week
financing.pmms30.note: Week of 2026-11-05. The 2026 average to date is 6.53 percent (financing.pmms30_2026_avg).

financing.pmms30_2026_avg.label: 30-year fixed mortgage rate, 2026 average
financing.pmms30_2026_avg.note: Mean of the 44 weekly values from 2026-01-08 to 2026-11-05. This is the rate the tract-level report uses.

financing.heloc_rate.label: Home equity line of credit rate, national average
financing.heloc_rate.note: Variable, moves with the prime rate (7.00 percent since 2026-09-16).

financing.presets.label: Ways to pay

all_borrowed.label: All borrowed at the 2026 average rate (report test)

financing.presets.note: ltc is loan to cost. The rest is cash. HELOC is shown as a 20-year amortizing loan and assumes enough home equity. Construction-to-perm spread of 0.5 point and 80 percent loan to cost are typical lender terms, not a published figure. FHA 203(k) needs an owner-occupied house and lender approval of the ADU.

operating.vacancy.label: Rental vacancy
operating.vacancy.note: Census Housing Vacancy Survey, Q3 2026. Metro values have wide margins (Philadelphia plus or minus 2.7 points, Pittsburgh plus or minus 3.6).

sources.title: Census HVS rental vacancy by metro, 2026
Census HVS rental vacancy by state, 2026

operating.management.label: Property management fee
operating.management.note: Only charged when the owner does not manage the unit (scenario self_managed false). Managers charge 8 to 12 percent plus a leasing fee.

sources.title: Baselane: how much do property managers charge

operating.maintenance.label: Maintenance and repairs reserve
operating.maintenance.note: Common rule of thumb. A brand-new unit may need less in the first years.

operating.insurance.label: Landlord insurance
operating.insurance.note: Median Pennsylvania landlord policy. Adding an ADU to the house policy may cost less. No source gives that increment.

operating.rental_license.label: Rental license or registration
operating.rental_license.note: Philadelphia rental license 69 per unit per year. Pittsburgh rental registry 16 per property + 5.50 permit inspection + 14 per unit. Elsewhere set by each town, taken as 0.

sources.title: City of Pittsburgh PLI 2026 fee schedule

tax.assessed_share_of_build_cost.label: Added market value the assessor puts on the unit
tax.assessed_share_of_build_cost.unit: share of build cost (mid hard cost, before soft costs)
tax.assessed_share_of_build_cost.note: Assessors value new construction mostly by cost. Soft costs, site work and contingency are left out. Owner judgement.

tax.philadelphia.rate.label: Philadelphia real estate tax rate
tax.philadelphia.rate.unit: share of assessed market value per year
tax.philadelphia.rate.note: City 0.6159 percent + School District 0.7839 percent. Unchanged since 2016 and kept for 2027.

sources.title: City of Philadelphia: lower your property tax bill ahead of 2027 valuations

tax.philadelphia.abatement.label: Philadelphia 10-year abatement for new residential construction
tax.philadelphia.abatement.unit: share of added value not taxed, by year
tax.philadelphia.abatement.note: Code 19-1303.4. For applications after 2021-12-31 the abated share falls 10 points a year. Apply within 60 days of the building permit. No change found in the 2026 or 2027 budgets. Whether an ADU counts as a new dwelling unit (this rule) or an improvement (Code 19-1303(2): 100 percent for 10 years, owner-occupied or for sale only) is decided by the Office of Property Assessment. Taken to cover both City and School tax (inferred from the 2018 city study, not stated in current rules).

sources.title: OPA application: abatement for new residential construction
OPA application: abatement for residential improvements

tax.pittsburgh.millage.label: Pittsburgh property tax millage, 2026
tax.pittsburgh.millage.note: Allegheny County 6.43 (up from 4.73 in 2025), City of Pittsburgh 9.67 (up from 8.06 for 2026), Pittsburgh Public Schools 10.457. Total 26.557 mills. Whether the city figure includes the 0.25 mill library and 0.50 mill parks levies was not confirmed.

sources.title: Allegheny County municipal millage profile, Pittsburgh

tax.pittsburgh.assessment_ratio.label: Allegheny County assessed value as a share of market value
tax.pittsburgh.assessment_ratio.note: Allegheny still assesses at 2012 base-year values. A new unit is valued as if built in 2012, so its assessed value is about the common level ratio times today's value. 2025 common level ratio approved by the State Tax Equalization Board on 2026-05-20.

sources.title: Allegheny Institute: Allegheny County's CLR continues its decline
WPRDC Allegheny County property assessment user guide (2012 base year)

tax.pittsburgh.reassessment.label: When Allegheny County adds a new unit to the tax roll

table.timing: interim assessment for the year the unit is finished

tax.pittsburgh.reassessment.note: 53 Pa.C.S. 8817 lets assessors change a value when improvements are made. The county reviews building, demolition and occupancy permits. Interim valuations are for major improvements, filed within 12 months of completion, valued as if the work stood on January 1. The model taxes the unit from year 1.

sources.title: Allegheny County: building permits and assessments

tax.pittsburgh.abatement.label: Pittsburgh abatement for a new rental unit
tax.pittsburgh.abatement.unit: share of added value not taxed, by year
tax.pittsburgh.abatement.note: City Code Chapters 265, 267 and 268 replaced Act 42 and LERTA in 2020 (apply within 180 days of the permit, 60 dollar fee). Chapter 267 reportedly gives a 3-year credit for rental property, but the terms were not verified in the primary text, so no abatement is applied.

sources.title: City of Pittsburgh real estate tax abatement application (Chapters 265 and 267)

tax.rest_of_pa.effective_rate.label: Pennsylvania median effective property tax rate
tax.rest_of_pa.effective_rate.unit: share of market value per year
tax.rest_of_pa.effective_rate.note: Statewide 2024. Counties vary a lot. Replace with a county rate when one is available.

sources.title: Tax Foundation: property taxes by state and county, 2026

value.cap_rate.label: Capitalization rate for the added value estimate
value.cap_rate.note: Mid is the Philadelphia multifamily average for Q3 2026. Low and high are the suburban class A and value-add rates from a lender survey. Used for Pittsburgh and the rest of the state too. A backyard unit does not sell on its own, so an appraiser may give it less.

sources.title: Matthews: Philadelphia multifamily market report Q3 2026
Apartment Loan Store: Philadelphia cap rates

verdict.rules.label: Verdict rules
verdict.rules.note: With a loan: pays when monthly cash flow at the mid cost is 0 or more and debt service coverage is at least dscr_pays. Close when it does not pay but cash flow at the low cost is 0 or more, or the mid-cost shortfall is within close_band of the monthly rent. Otherwise does not pay. Paid in cash: pays when yield on cost is at least the 30-year mortgage rate (what the money could save by not borrowing). Close when the yield is within close_band of that rate or the low-cost yield clears it. Taxes in the test are the average of the first 10 years (avg10), so the Philadelphia abatement counts but does not dominate. Other options: year1, full. The 1.20 coverage is a common lender minimum. The 10 percent band matches the tract report.

pro_forma.schedule_years.label: Years shown in the tax schedule
pro_forma.schedule_years.note: Covers the 10-year abatement and two years after.

tract.growth.cpi_u.label: CPI-U yearly average, used to put ACS dollars in 2024 dollars
tract.growth.cpi_u.note: ACS 5-year dollars are in the last year of the window, so 2010-14 values are deflated with 2014, 2015-19 with 2019 and 2020-24 with 2024. Used by pipeline/tract/growth.py.

sources.title: BLS CPI for All Urban Consumers, U.S. city average, all items (CUUR0000SA0), annual averages

tract.growth.min_start.label: Smallest starting value for a tract growth rate
tract.growth.min_start.note: Tiny bases give wild yearly rates. A rate is left blank when the start is under these values. Set in the course notebooks, kept here so the modules and notebooks agree.

tract.payoff.size_sqft.label: Unit size in the tract payoff test
tract.payoff.size_sqft.note: One-bedroom backyard unit. The tool's base case (1 BR, 600 sq ft, one story) uses the same size.

tract.payoff.hard_psf.label: Build cost per sq ft in the tract payoff test
tract.payoff.hard_psf.note: A simple all-in rate for the statewide tract screen. The lot-level money model builds cost from parts instead (cost.hard_psf.detached_new plus site work, utilities, contingency and soft costs). The mid value matches the Terner Center median.

sources.title: Terner Center California ADU survey (median 250 per sq ft, 2020 prices)
Cost to Build House: ADU cost in Pennsylvania (600 sq ft: Philadelphia 313 to 363, Pittsburgh 297 per sq ft all-in)

tract.payoff.soft_share.label: Soft costs in the tract payoff test
tract.payoff.soft_share.note: Design, permits and fees on top of the build cost.

tract.payoff.loan_years.label: Loan length in the tract payoff test
tract.payoff.loan_years.note: All of the cost is borrowed. The rate is financing.pmms30_2026_avg in the main run and financing.pmms30 in the sensitivity table.

tract.payoff.opex_share.label: Operating costs in the tract payoff test
tract.payoff.opex_share.note: Vacancy, repairs, property tax and insurance as one share of rent. The lot-level model itemizes these instead.

tract.payoff.close_band.label: Band for a 'maybe' in the tract payoff test
tract.payoff.close_band.note: maybe = net rent covers the payment at the low build cost, or is within this share of the payment at the mid cost.

tract.payoff.rent_basis.label: Rent used in the tract payoff test
tract.payoff.rent_basis.note: rent_b1 = tract median gross rent (ACS 2020-24, B25064) times the county ratio of 1-bedroom to all-unit median rent (B25031). Where the tract has no median rent it is the county 1-bedroom median. It is the same column the tool uses. Cross-checks: raw tract B25031 1-bedroom median (often blank), HUD SAFMR 1-bedroom by ZIP joined to tracts through the LODES block crosswalk, and the all-unit median the first report used.

tract.forecast.permits_per_100k.label: ADU permits per 100,000 people per year in cities that allow ADUs by right
tract.forecast.permits_per_100k.note: Range from the project proposal, credited there to Pew research on permissive cities. The exact page was not recorded. Confirm the source before the report goes out.

sources.title: Project proposal figure, credited to The Pew Charitable Trusts (page not recorded)

tract.forecast.pays_weight.label: Share of the permit rate by payoff class
tract.forecast.pays_weight.note: No is not zero: some people build for family, not rent. Tracts with no rent data take the no weight.

tract.forecast.rule_factor.label: Share of the permit rate under each town rule
tract.forecast.rule_factor.note: Rules come from shared/legal_status.csv. Under a state bill every town it reaches counts as allowed.

tract.forecast.unlisted_rule.label: Rule for towns not in legal_status.csv
tract.forecast.unlisted_rule.note: Many PA towns allow some kind of in-law unit but are not coded yet. This choice drives most of the gap between today and a state bill.

tract.forecast.lots_index_cap.label: Cap on the lots-with-room index
tract.forecast.lots_index_cap.note: Share of homes on a lot with room, divided by the state share, is capped here so a few tracts do not dominate.

tract.forecast.legal_class_factor.label: Share of the permit rate by town legal class (from the rule files)
tract.forecast.legal_class_factor.note: Classes come from adu.status in shared/rules (pipeline/tract/legal.py). Discretionary, family-only, conversion-only and unknown keep the old 'limited' factor, so a change in the totals comes from a town's class and not from new factors. 'none' (code silent or prohibits ADUs) leaves only a variance, so it is near zero. Under a state bill every town it reaches counts as by_right.

lots.flag.steep_slope_min_share.label: Steep slope flag: share of the lot in the layer
lots.flag.steep_slope_min_share.note: Steep slope areas are mapped coarsely, so a lot is flagged only when a real part of it (a quarter) is inside.

lots.terrain.moderate_slope_pct.label: Ground slope: moderate from this mean slope under the unit
lots.terrain.moderate_slope_pct.note: Under about 15 percent a small house sits on ordinary footings with light grading. From 15 to 25 percent it usually needs stepped or deeper foundations, retaining walls or more grading, and many hillside ordinances start their review here. Reported next to the fit (terrain.slope_class); the fit itself does not change.

sources.title: Owner setting (terrain refresh, pipeline/terrain.py), from common hillside practice

lots.terrain.steep_slope_pct.label: Ground slope: steep from this mean slope under the unit
lots.terrain.steep_slope_pct.note: At 25 percent or more ground is steep: engineered foundations, a geotechnical look and grading permits are likely, and building costs rise sharply. Pittsburgh maps slopes of 25 percent or more as its steep slope layer (PGHWebSlope25). Sets terrain.steep_site and the gentle fit (best spot searched only on buildable ground under this slope). The fit's yes or no does not change.

sources.title: Owner setting (terrain refresh, pipeline/terrain.py), matching the City of Pittsburgh 25 percent slope layer

lots.flag.landslide_min_share.label: Landslide flag: share of the lot in the layer
lots.flag.landslide_min_share.note: Landslide areas are mapped coarsely, so a lot is flagged only when a real part of it (a quarter) is inside.

lots.flag.flood_min_share.label: Flood flag: share of the lot in the floodplain
lots.flag.flood_min_share.note: Any sizable floodplain share matters for where a unit can sit, so 10 percent is enough.

lots.flag.historic_min_share.label: Historic flag: share of the lot in a district
lots.flag.historic_min_share.note: A historic district covers whole blocks, so half the lot inside means the lot is in the district. The lot center in a district also counts.

lots.garage.min_sqft.label: Smallest accessory building read as a garage
lots.garage.min_sqft.note: A one-car garage is about 10 x 18 ft. Smaller accessory buildings are sheds, which the fit treats as removable.

lots.garage.min_gap_ft.label: Strict garage test: gap from the house
lots.garage.min_gap_ft.note: Where a place asks for the strict test (Philadelphia, where most accessory outlines are additions and lean-tos), a garage stands at least this far from the house.

lots.garage.behind_tol_ft.label: Strict garage test: how far in front of the house's rear face
lots.garage.behind_tol_ft.note: The center of a garage sits no more than this in front of the house's rear face.

lots.garage.access_ft.label: Strict garage test: distance to a street, alley or driveway
lots.garage.access_ft.note: A garage has a street, alley or driveway this close.

lots.accessory_clearance_ft.label: Clearance between a new unit and a garage or shed
lots.accessory_clearance_ft.note: Planning clearance. Under 5 ft a facing wall needs a fire rating (the rule files' fire_separation.rated_wall_below_ft is used when present). Two dwellings keep the larger separation_ft from the rules.

lots.party_wall.tol_ft.label: Party wall: distance from the side lot line
lots.party_wall.tol_ft.note: A side lot line the main house runs along, within this distance, is shared with the attached neighbor and gets no side yard. Only for twins, rows and multi-unit houses.

lots.party_wall.min_ft.label: Party wall: length along the side lot line
lots.party_wall.min_ft.note: The house must run along the side line for at least this length (or half the line) to count as a party wall.

lots.story_ft.label: Height per story when no height is measured
lots.story_ft.note: Used only when a building has the assessor's story count and no measured height.

lots.street_search_ft.label: Search distance for the streets that front a lot
lots.street_search_ft.note: Streets within this distance of a lot are used to find its front.

lots.fallback_setbacks_ft.label: Setbacks used when the rule files give none
lots.fallback_setbacks_ft.note: Used only for a district outside the rule tables. Every use is listed in the record's assumed list and cited as a planning assumption, never as law.
